## Standard Evaluation Report (SE)

What the certifier receives: a `period`, a `scope` boundary, the `results`, a `rollup`, `coverage`, and a name against them via `signOff`.

```ts
import { StandardEvaluationReport } from '@cardstack/catalog/cards/audit/standard-evaluation-report';
@field lastReport = linksTo(() => StandardEvaluationReport);
```

**Findings are not stored here.** They live on the results that raised them and are read back by walking `results`, so a finding can never be closed in one place and still read open in another. The product spec kept a separate `findings` list; one copy is worth more than two views of it, and this is the deviation to know about.

**`coverage` counts conclusive verdicts over rules that applied**, so a run full of `unproven` reports thin coverage rather than a clean bill. That is the single most common way a compliance dashboard flatters itself, and the number is computed rather than entered.

**`signOffBlocked` holds the certificate.** A report with an open finding that puts the certificate at risk says so in the isolated view, and the second approval step is meant to be held on it. Sign-off is the existing Approval Chain block, consumed unchanged.

## Example
The linked example is the FY26 H2 supplier run: two subjects, eight results, one critical finding open, 86% coverage, rolled up to **fail**. Its numbers are the real output of the engine against the realm's two Vendor Profile cards, not illustrative figures.

## Non-goals
Does not run the audit — Audit writes the results and links them here. Does not issue a certificate; it links the Document when one arrives. No period-over-period comparison yet: recurrence is tracked on the finding.
